I was talking to my roommate today, and he brought up the new iPod. He was interested in getting it, but I personally don't have a need for one anymore. I've completely gone to streaming for all of my music. I solely use Spotify now.

When my contract was up, I switched to T-Mobile. They don't charge music streaming against your data. Prior to that, I'd burn my 3 gigs streaming music within the first two weeks of the month. I would have a few playlists saved on my phone, for once I ran out of data. Since I live in an area that T-Mobile covers rather well, I don't even do that anymore. I typically have my music all the time.

This leaves me to pose two questions:

Do you prefer to stream or have direct ownership of you music?

Do you still use media devices like the iPod? (Music stored directly to the device)

I use both, in that I can get the best of both worlds and I am able to tweak my listening experience to what I want at that given time. I think that they both have their pro's and con's and I try to use both as best as I can to give myself the best possible listening experience I can.

If I was biased to side, it will be direct ownership, as I have a love for vinyl that borders on insanity.

I prefer to own my music. Be it digital, CDs, vinyl, or even tape. Even though I rarely listen to the source media after ripping / converting it to digital, I like having the physical thing, the piece of art.

I don’t use any of the streaming services, although I have a sizeable library on Bandcamp (which has an app for streaming albums you’ve bought). I use it occasionally if I’m on mobile or someone else’s computer and don’t have my files.

I haven’t used an iPod or other dedicated music player in years. Most of the time I’m listening on my desktop/laptop. I do fancy getting a dedicated device in the future, if I can find one with huge storage size and preferably open-source firmware, so I can bring my music everywhere and not be tied to my computers or phone.
There are tons of high fidelity players that do this and have expandable memory! And some a reasonably priced ($30-90) though the "fidelity" wouldn't be at the same level compared to a $400 device.

Yeah, I’m aware of quite a few choices, from iPod knockoffs, cheap Android devices, to “audiophile” players. It’s just not a priority purchase at all, more a luxury thing.

I also haven’t seen any particular one that stands out from the crowd with the right combination of looks and features. If I get one I want to be using it for many years, like my original iPod which I loved, only now my standards are much higher — it needs to be futureproof in terms of expandable storage, replaceable batteries, and open-source firmware.
Check out ibasso dx90. Expandable storage, replaceable batteries, and you can mod the firmware with rockbox. Some have it modded to mimic iPods.

I've been a big fan of Spotify ever since I found it two months ago, but depending on your music preferences there can be unexpected benefits to owning over streaming. In my teenage years I came to be a big fan of Japanese music. They have a very active music industry there, but sadly it is very difficult for anyone outside of Japan to buy the music, and as far as I know, impossible to stream just the songs you want on any service available in the Unites States. There is a Japanese section of the iTunes Store, but for all intents and purposes it is region locked (You must have a Japanese address to register and also need to buy Japanese iTunes cards). Eventually I was able to make a Japanese iTunes account by purchasing an iTunes card on a website and using a Japanese address they provided, but back then there was no streaming as we know it today. Suffice to say I bought digital copies of all the songs I wanted and still have them to this day even though that account is most certainly inactive. When I joined Spotify I immediately tried to find my favorite Japanese artists, but could only find a handful of American covers of their songs. This is just one example of how owning can be beneficial.
